1.title: Marl-Sandstone: A Mixed-Texture, Diverse Terroir
1.html: The marl-sandstone (marno-gréseux) family is made of Jurassic Dogger sandy marl, or Tertiary sandstone / limestone gravel deposits, with a texture between pure limestone and pure sandstone. It has 7 Grand Crus and is one of the most widely distributed geological families in Alsace.
2.title: The Seven Marl-Sandstone Stars (Part 1)
2.items.0.label: Furstentum (Kientzheim & Sigolsheim, 30.50 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Lower Dogger marl-limestone-sandstone, slopes up to 37%, a "limestone island" with Mediterranean-type vegetation. Documented in 1330 in Basel monastery records. Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris, combining power and finesse.
2.items.1.label: Kirchberg de Ribeauvillé (Ribeauvillé, 11.40 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Lower Muschelkalk dolomitic marl plus upper calcareous marl, clayey stony soil. Documented in 1328. Mainly Riesling and Muscat, with Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris also good; the elegant aromas typical of marl-limestone unfold over time.
2.items.2.label: Ollwiller (Wuenheim, 35.86 ha)
2.items.2.desc: Tertiary sandy-clayey sediments, one of the driest areas in France (only 450 mm a year on average). A 12th-century castle bears witness to its long history. Mainly Riesling and Gewurztraminer, with flavours fully open after 2–3 years of ageing.
2.items.3.label: Pfersigberg (Eguisheim & Wettolsheim, 74.55 ha)
2.items.3.desc: Gravelly limestone base (hard grey Muschelkalk gravel or yellow Jurassic gravel), alkaline rendzina soil (pH 7.7–8). Documented in the 16th century and revived at Colmar's first wine fair in 1927. The "land of choice" for Gewurztraminer, with Pinot Gris, Riesling and Muscat also excellent.
3.title: The Seven Marl-Sandstone Stars (Part 2)
3.items.0.label: Saering (Guebwiller, 26.75 ha)
3.items.0.desc: Oligocene Latdorfian conglomerate with interbedded marl, heavy marl-sandy soil. Documented in 1250 and sold under its own brand from 1830. Riesling takes priority, with typical floral character, dry and with a clear backbone.
3.items.1.label: Spiegel (Bergholtz & Guebwiller, 18.26 ha)
3.items.1.desc: Oligocene conglomerate (mainly sandstone gravel) with interbedded marl, sandy-clayey soil with good water retention. A reputation of 50+ years. Mainly Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris, with excellent Riesling and Muscat on south-facing slopes; Pinot Gris is especially full and round.
3.items.2.label: Vorbourg (Rouffach & Westhalten, 73.61 ha)
3.items.2.desc: Sandstone and oolitic limestone gravel marl soil, with a surface cover of loess. Extremely early ripening and often develops noble rot naturally. A record of 762 shows Bishop Heddo donating an ancient vineyard. Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat all suit it, with age bringing peach, apricot and hazelnut aromas.
4.question: What is the outstanding climatic feature of the Ollwiller (Wuenheim) site?
4.options.0: It is the site with the highest rainfall in Alsace
4.options.1: Annual rainfall averages only about 450 mm, making it one of the driest areas in France
4.options.2: It is the most strongly influenced by maritime climate
4.options.3: It is the only site with a frost risk
4.explanation: Ollwiller sits in a valley sheltered by the Freundstein and Vieil-Armand peaks, which block the prevailing winds, so annual rainfall averages only about 450 mm and it is one of the driest areas in France — one reason it makes an interesting contrast with Vorbourg of the same family (which naturally develops noble rot).
5.keyPoints.0: The marl-sandstone family has 7 sites, the widest distribution, with a texture between limestone and sandstone
5.keyPoints.1: Furstentum: 37% slope, a "limestone island" with Mediterranean-type vegetation
5.keyPoints.2: Pfersigberg (74.55 ha): the land of choice for Gewurztraminer, alkaline rendzina soil
5.keyPoints.3: Ollwiller: only 450 mm of rain a year, one of the driest areas in France
5.keyPoints.4: Vorbourg (73.61 ha): extremely early ripening, often develops noble rot naturally
